name: King of the North
overview: The King of the North is a male figure identified as one of the four kings mentioned in Daniel 11:6. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe, lineage, or personal background. His role is primarily defined by his position among these four kings.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of the North' means 'prince of the north' and serves as a descriptive designation rather than a personal name. This title is not given by God but is used in Daniel 11:6 to distinguish this ruler geographically and politically.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of the North beyond his identification as one of the four kings in Daniel 11:6. There are no known connections to other individuals or tribes listed.
scriptureSignificance: The King of the North holds significance as a key political figure in the prophetic vision of Daniel 11, representing one of four kings whose actions and interactions are part of God's sovereign plan. His mention underscores the unfolding of divine purposes in history, emphasizing God's control over earthly kingdoms and events.
